brain-listening.brain3_listening_baselin: Your mastery level is already high, so we are starting with a challenge: fast pace, limited replays, and long clips.
Your mastery level is still low, so we are starting with the easiest combination: slow speed, full replays, and short clips.
Moderate mastery level, so starting at the middle of the difficulty ladder.
brain-listening.brain3_listening_ceiling: All dimensions are already at their hardest level; nothing more can be increased.
brain-listening.brain3_listening_default: No listening data is available to read yet, so difficulty is set to a safe midpoint: natural speed, 2 replays, medium clips.
brain-listening.brain3_listening_floor: All dimensions are already at their easiest level; nothing more can be decreased.
brain-listening.brain3_listening_hidden_: Accuracy is high, but an average of >= 2 replays indicates the student is working much harder than it appears — increases are held back until the cognitive load drops.
brain-listening.brain3_listening_hold_in: Accuracy is within the target band (±0.1), so difficulty is maintained — this is where learning is most efficient.
brain-listening.brain3_listening_insuffi: Evidence in the recent window is too thin to trust, so difficulty is held steady — a policy that swings based on a single answer is more dangerous than standing still.
brain-listening.brain3_listening_step_do: Accuracy is below target and replays are maxed out, so the clip is shortened by one level.
Accuracy is below target despite full replays and short clips, so the speed is slowed down by one band.
Accuracy is below target, so the safety net is restored first: the replay quota increases by one — the cheapest adjustment, leaving the material unchanged.
brain-listening.brain3_listening_step_up: Accuracy is well above target and speed is already at maximum, so clip length is increased by one level.
Accuracy is well above target, so playback speed is increased by one band — speed only, so if results change we know exactly which knob caused it.
Accuracy is well above target at maximum speed and clip length, so the final safety net is reduced: the replay quota decreases by one.
brain-olm.calib-neutral: Your predicted confidence ({pred}%) and actual outcome ({actual}%) are well-aligned. Keep up the habit of estimating before answering — that habit is what keeps your calibration sharp.
brain-olm.calib-over: You predicted {pred}% right, but your actual score was {actual}%. Before answering, try to state your reasoning first — if you cannot articulate the reason, lower your confidence estimate.
brain-olm.calib-under: You predicted {pred}% right, but your actual score was {actual}%. Your answers are more accurate than your estimates — once you recognize the pattern, dare to raise your confidence estimate.
brain-olm.miscon-generic: For {concept}, there is a repeating answer pattern that needs to be retested.
brain-olm.miscon-pair: For {concept}, you repeatedly used the form «{wrong}» instead of the standard form «{right}». This pattern will be retested in the next practice session.
brain-olm.miscon-wrong-only: For {concept}, your answer pattern repeatedly leans toward «{wrong}». This pattern will be retested in the next practice session.

brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_baseline_: Mastery is already high, so the starting point is immediately challenging: full sentences with no assistance.
Mastery is still low, so the starting point uses the easiest combination: single words, with a spoken model provided first.
Mastery is moderate, so the starting point is in the middle of the ladder: cued phrases.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_ceiling: Both dimensions are already at their hardest level; nothing more can be increased.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_default: No speaking data is available to read yet, so difficulty is set to a safe midpoint: cued phrase prompts.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_evidence_: Coverage is high, but the latency is impossibly short for human speech production — the recognizer almost certainly misread it; this evidence is barely counted.

The student replayed the example repeatedly before speaking — getting it right after many examples is not proof of the same ability as getting it right on the first hearing; the kappa score is discounted further.
High coverage with humanly reasonable latency — usable production evidence, still adjusted with a speaking discount.
Low coverage or very long latency — the student struggled or the recognizer only captured a part of it; the evidence weight is small.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_floor: Both dimensions are already at their easiest level; nothing more can be decreased.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_hidden_ef: Coverage is high, but the very long latency indicates the student is working much harder than it appears — increases are held back until production becomes fluent.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_hold_in_b: Coverage is within the target band (±0.1), so difficulty is maintained — this is where practice is most efficient.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_insuffici: Evidence in the recent window is too thin to trust, so difficulty is held steady — a policy that swings based on a single attempt is more dangerous than standing still.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_noisy_evi: Most of the recent evidence is suspicious (high coverage with impossibly short latency) — likely a recognizer reading error, so difficulty is held steady rather than raised based on false evidence.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_step_down: Coverage is below target even though a model was spoken first, so prompt complexity is decreased by one level.
Coverage is below target, so the scaffold is stepped down one level — easiest button, the material remains unchanged.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_step_up_c: Coverage is stably above target and the student is speaking without help, so the prompt complexity goes up one level.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_step_up_s: Coverage is stably above target, so the scaffold is removed one level — material unchanged, so we know the student is doing the work, not the scaffold.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_target_no: No weak lessons recorded, so speaking practice is open with no specific skill target.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_target_pr: All prerequisite weak lessons are not yet solid, so there is no specific target — strengthen the prerequisites first through other modes before forcing verbal production.
brain-speaking.brain3_speaking_target_we: 練習 target is taken from the weakest lesson with solid prerequisites — practicing production on an unestablished foundation only trains the feeling of failure.

login.pesan-01-headline: Hey {name}, your goal of studying abroad is awesome. But have you studied today yet? 👀
login.pesan-01-lead: Scholarships and your dream tech university aren't built on good intentions alone. Let's grind for 10–15 minutes—small steps, big impact.
login.pesan-02-headline: Bro, want to study IT abroad? English isn't just a side quest 😭
login.pesan-02-lead: IELTS/TOEFL will be one of the main gateways. Since you're still a freshman, build your skills now so you won't panic as a sophomore.
login.pesan-03-headline: {name}, are you really losing to your FYP feed over just 5 問? 💀
login.pesan-03-lead: You don't need to pretend to be productive for an hour. Just get five answers right that you actually understand, then you can go back to your day.
login.pesan-04-headline: Plot twist: sophomore {name} will thank today's {name}.
login.pesan-04-lead: If you build the foundation now, your future IELTS/TOEFL prep will just be leveling up—not starting from scratch.
login.pesan-05-headline: Hey, international scholarships don't just drop out of the sky 😭
login.pesan-05-lead: What you can control right now is simple: show up, practice, understand your mistakes, and repeat tomorrow.
login.pesan-06-headline: Being lazy is valid. Skipping studying every day? Now that's dangerous.
login.pesan-06-lead: When your energy is running low, lower your goal. One review or five 問 still counts as progress.
login.pesan-07-headline: You want to study IT abroad, right? Well, prove it a little today.
login.pesan-07-lead: English will be used for lectures, documentation, discussions, internships, and even interviews. So this is an investment, not a random chore.
login.pesan-08-headline: Hey {name}, don't just have a “main character dream”, have a main character routine too 😭
login.pesan-08-lead: Big goals need small, consistent routines. Today, just finish one FIEZEL session.
login.pesan-09-headline: Friendly reminder: your future doesn't need a perfectionist version of you, it needs a consistent one.
login.pesan-09-lead: You don't have to be great today. The important thing is that your skills move up one step compared to yesterday.
login.pesan-10-headline: Grade 11 IELTS sounds far away? That's the trap, bro.
login.pesan-10-lead: This Grade 10 time is actually great for building vocab, grammar, reading, and habits without being chased by a deadline.
login.pesan-11-headline: {name}, saying “I'll do it later” adds up to an entire semester 😭
login.pesan-11-lead: Open a session right now. Let the skills pile up later, not the excuses.
login.pesan-12-headline: You don't need to be Einstein today. Just don't ghost FIEZEL 👻
login.pesan-12-lead: Leave behind at least one piece of study evidence: finished 問, reviewed vocab, or completed reading.
login.pesan-13-headline: Bro, getting answers wrong isn't embarrassing. That's free data.
login.pesan-13-lead: The important thing is not just looking at the answer. Figure out why you got it wrong, because that's how FIEZEL can make your next practice even more precise.
login.pesan-14-headline: Want a scholarship? Your skills need a receipt, not just a wishlist.
login.pesan-14-lead: 進捗 recorded today is way more useful than the promise of “studying seriously tomorrow.”
login.pesan-15-headline: Hey, your brain needs maintenance too. Even a laptop gets updates 😭
login.pesan-15-lead: Review the material you're starting to forget. A little repetition now means you won't have to relearn from scratch later.
login.pesan-16-headline: {name}, when you're feeling super lazy: deal, just 5 問.
login.pesan-16-lead: If you're still exhausted after five 問, stop. But don't let today be completely empty.
login.pesan-17-headline: Your English doesn't have to look amazing right away. The important thing is that the graph goes up.
login.pesan-17-lead: FIEZEL cares more about long-term patterns than one impressive session.
login.pesan-18-headline: Studying IT abroad = cool. Reading documentation without translating every 2 lines = cooler.
login.pesan-18-lead: The vocabulary and reading skills you build now will still be useful long after the exams are over.
login.pesan-19-headline: Bro, don't wait for your study mood to show up.
login.pesan-19-lead: Start with just 10 minutes. Usually, your brain only starts focusing after your body gets moving.
login.pesan-20-headline: Today, do you want to be “future me will study” or “past me already studied”? 👀
login.pesan-20-lead: Choose the second one. One small session is enough to keep your rhythm going.
login.pesan-21-headline: {name}, Grade 11 is going to arrive whether you're ready or not 😭
login.pesan-21-lead: That's why we build up our skills now, so IELTS/TOEFL later feels like the next level, not a sudden boss fight.
login.pesan-22-headline: If your goal is abroad, don't treat English like just a school subject.
login.pesan-22-lead: Turn it into an everyday skill: read, understand patterns, recall words, and dare to make mistakes.
login.pesan-23-headline: Hey, it's a waste to let your study streak die just because of “later.”
login.pesan-23-lead: Open FIEZEL, finish your minimum target, and then feel free to move on to other activities.
login.pesan-24-headline: You don't need to study for a long time. You need to study often enough.
login.pesan-24-lead: 15 minutes of consistency can be more effective than a two-hour marathon followed by disappearing for a week.
login.pesan-25-headline: {name}, scholarships love proof. And your brain loves repetition.
login.pesan-25-lead: So today we're giving you both: tracked progress and material that actually sticks.
login.pesan-26-headline: No pressure, but… big dreams still require small daily work 😭
login.pesan-26-lead: Pick your weakest area and sort it out a little. We'll continue tomorrow.
login.pesan-27-headline: Hey, don't be scared of the messy parts on the learning map.
login.pesan-27-lead: That's not a report card of failure. That's a GPS showing you the fastest route to level up.
login.pesan-28-headline: Grammar driving you crazy? Relax, let's find the pattern—no memorizing textbooks.
login.pesan-28-lead: Pay attention to time clues, sentence functions, and why the other options are wrong. It'll slowly start clicking automatically.
login.pesan-29-headline: Don't just guess on reading, bestie 😭 find the evidence.
login.pesan-29-lead: Get used to pointing out the sentence or clue that supports your answer. That's a skill you'll really need on the test.
login.pesan-30-headline: Hey {name}, 10 minutes right now can save you 2 hours of panic later.
login.pesan-30-lead: Do your due reviews before the material completely fades from your memory.
login.pesan-31-headline: Your goal isn't to "look hardworking." Your goal is to actually get good.
login.pesan-31-lead: So no need to just chase numbers. Understand a few 問 seriously, then move on.
login.pesan-32-headline: Just logging into FIEZEL doesn't count as studying, bro 😭
login.pesan-32-lead: Leave behind at least five meaningful answers so today's visit is actual progress.
login.pesan-33-headline: Future {name} is waiting for a skill delivery from you today 📦
login.pesan-33-lead: Send just a little: a few vocab words, one grammar lesson, or one reading. The important thing is keeping the package moving.
login.pesan-34-headline: You've got a study-abroad target. FIEZEL has one question: what are you doing today to get closer?
login.pesan-34-lead: No need for a dramatic answer. One focused session is enough.
login.pesan-35-headline: Hey {name}, it's fine to chill. Just don't disappear from practice for too long 😭
login.pesan-35-lead: Consistency > intensity. Come back before the break turns into a habit.
login.pesan-36-headline: One empty day won't make you fail. But coming back today makes a difference.
login.pesan-36-lead: No lectures. Just pick a focus, do a little bit, and you're done.
login.pesan-37-headline: Morning, {name}. Your brain is at its freshest around this time.
login.pesan-37-lead: Before notifications pile up and the day gets noisy, grab a session. Morning sessions usually actually get finished.
login.pesan-38-headline: It's late, but there's still room for one small session.
login.pesan-38-lead: Keep it light. A ten-minute vocab review will still lock in what you learned today.
login.pesan-39-headline: The weekend isn't an excuse to quit, but it's also not an excuse to force it.
login.pesan-39-lead: Cut your target in half. The goal is to keep the streak alive, not to become insanely productive today.
login.pesan-40-headline: Monday again. Skip the drama, just open one session.
login.pesan-40-lead: A neat week usually starts with a first day you don't skip. Five 問 are enough to start.
login.pesan-41-headline: The calendar keeps moving, and the semester waits for no one.
login.pesan-41-lead: Freshman year, first semester is the freest time you'll ever have. Use it now, not later.
login.pesan-42-headline: Skipped yesterday? Whatever. The real mistake is skipping two days in a row.
login.pesan-42-lead: No punishments here. Open one session, reconnect the streak, and let's keep going like nothing happened.
login.pesan-43-headline: Your study streak is going. It'd be such a waste to break it over ten minutes of laziness.
login.pesan-43-lead: What builds your skills isn't your best day, but the ordinary days you still show up for.
login.pesan-44-headline: 戻る after a long ghosting phase? ようこそ back, nobody's taking attendance.
login.pesan-44-lead: Start with the easy stuff to get your confidence back first. The hard levels can wait.
login.pesan-45-headline: Vocabulary is fuel. Without it, your grammar is just an empty shell.
login.pesan-45-lead: Ten words that truly stick are more useful than a hundred words that just pass by.
login.pesan-46-headline: Grammar isn't for memorization; it's for making sure you're heard.
login.pesan-46-lead: Clear sentences keep people focused on the content of your message, not how you're saying it.
login.pesan-47-headline: Your listening skills will be tested in real classes, not just on tests.
login.pesan-47-lead: Foreign professors speak quickly and don't repeat themselves. Train your ears now, not when you're already there.
login.pesan-48-headline: Speaking is a physical skill. Your mouth needs practice, not just your brain.
login.pesan-48-lead: Talking to yourself in your room counts. What matters is that your voice comes out, instead of just reading in your head.
login.pesan-49-headline: Fast reading is what will save you when you're in college.
login.pesan-49-lead: IT college reading materials pile up and have no translations. 練習 now while the texts are still short.
login.pesan-50-headline: Mistakes are data, not a disgrace.
login.pesan-50-lead: Every wrong answer shows FIEZEL precisely where you are weak. That is actually what makes your practice targeted.
login.pesan-51-headline: Don't wait to understand everything before starting. It's never going to happen.
login.pesan-51-lead: Understanding comes after practice, not before. Just start with what you can do.
login.pesan-52-headline: Compare yourself to yesterday's {name}, not to people on TikTok.
login.pesan-52-lead: They don't show the failed processes. You have your own numbers on the Learning Map, and those don't lie.
login.pesan-53-headline: Perfectionism is just laziness disguised as a good excuse.
login.pesan-53-lead: A messy session that gets finished always beats a perfect session that never gets started.
login.pesan-54-headline: Don't wait for motivation to strike. Motivation comes later.
login.pesan-54-lead: Usually, a good mood only shows up after the first five 問. So just push through the uncomfortable part first.
login.pesan-55-headline: 進捗 often feels invisible from the inside.
login.pesan-55-lead: That's why the Learning Map exists. Trust the chart, not your feelings today.
login.pesan-56-headline: Reviewing is much cheaper than learning everything back from scratch.
login.pesan-56-lead: Ten minutes now saves an hour later. That's the compound interest version of learning.
login.pesan-57-headline: Understanding why you're wrong is much more valuable than a lucky correct guess.
login.pesan-57-lead: Read the explanation briefly. What you're building is understanding, not just a score.
login.pesan-58-headline: English in IT is a working language, not a school subject.
login.pesan-58-lead: Documentation, error messages, team discussions—everything is in English. You're practicing for work, not for a report card.
login.pesan-59-headline: Later on, there will be scholarship interviews you can't answer using Google Translate.
login.pesan-59-lead: The only thing that will save you then is the practice hours you've quietly accumulated starting from now.
login.pesan-60-headline: {name} from 2 grades ahead is watching you from the future.
login.pesan-60-lead: They aren't asking you to be a genius. They just ask that you don't waste a whole year.
login.pesan-61-headline: A great report card is a bonus. What you're chasing are skills you can actually use.
login.pesan-61-lead: It's a subtle difference, but the direction is vastly different. One stops on paper, the other follows you abroad.
login.pesan-62-headline: Big targets are just a pile of small days that weren't skipped.
login.pesan-62-lead: There is no single heroic day that gets you through. What gets you through are three hundred ordinary days.
login.pesan-63-headline: Be the person who keeps showing up even when you're not feeling it. That's it.
login.pesan-63-lead: It's not about being great today. It's about being someone you can rely on.
login.pesan-64-headline: Is your day heavy? It's okay to take it slow. But don't make it zero.
login.pesan-64-lead: Even a single review still counts. FIEZEL doesn't expect you to be a machine.
login.pesan-65-headline: Nobody's watching over you. That's the real test.
login.pesan-65-lead: What you're building right now isn't just English, but the habit of doing things without being told.
login.pesan-66-headline: Ten minutes. Then you're free to do whatever you want.
login.pesan-66-lead: Seriously, that's it. Open one session, finish it, and keep living without any guilt.

tutorv3.script-4: Let's put it on a timeline. The action starts before now, but the result reaches the present. That connection is the point.
tutorv3.script-6: Let's make it concrete. Imagine the key is still missing right now. The present perfect helps connect a previous event to a situation that still applies today.
tutorv3.script-7: You are separating two functions of the same verb. 'Went' is the simple past form. After 'have' or 'has', English requires the third form, so we say 'I have gone', not 'I have went'.
tutorv3.script-8: Use 'has' for he, she, and it. Use 'have' for I, you, we, and they. The meaning remains the same; the subject determines the auxiliary verb.
tutorv3.script-9: A useful question isn't just when the event happened. Ask whether the result is still connected to the present. If so, the present perfect is often the more appropriate choice.

voice.notice.quota.exhausted.silent: The audio cannot be played right now. The text is still here, and your allowance will reset after midnight.

voice.notice.quota.exhausted.title: Today's allowance has run out
voice.notice.quota.low.silent: The audio didn't play for this sentence. You can still read the text.
voice.notice.quota.low.spoken: Still sounding normal. If it runs out later, I'll switch to my backup voice.
voice.notice.quota.low.title: Today's voice quota is almost gone

voice.notice.quota.rate.slowdown.title: Tapped too fast in succession

voice.notice.service.degraded.title: The voice service is taking a short break

voice.notice.service.providerError.spoke: I'm using my backup voice for this sentence.
voice.notice.service.providerError.title: Failed to prepare the voice
voice.notice.service.unknown.silent: I couldn't play this sentence just yet. You can still read the text, and you can press Listen again.
voice.notice.service.unknown.spoken: I'll use my backup voice for now.
voice.notice.service.unknown.title: Voice is not yet available for this sentence
